newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana Stock Exchange ends week higher.
newsitem.headline: Ghana Stock Exchange ends week higher.

text.p: The Ghana Stock Exchange ended the week higher on Friday, with dealers saying signs of improved corporate results and a downturn in inflation were starting to filter through to investors.
The GSE All-Share Index rose 1.84 points to 379.88 from 378.04 on Wednesday and total market capitalisation rose to 3,281.69 from 3,274.51 billion cedis ($2 billion).
The index stood at 375.84 points last Friday, market capitalisation at 3,266.82 billion cedis.

"We are impressed by the corporate results filtering through the market. They are favourable indications for the equity market and investors have also started picking up the signals," one dealer said.
Ashanti Goldfields Co, Ghana's biggest company, climbed 50 cedis to 29,900, with dealers attributing the climb to a recent rise in the world price of gold.

Ghana Commercial Bank, the exchange's second biggest equity, rose 12 to 712 cedis. Earlier results showed 1996 first-half profits rising to 19.74 billion cedis from 12.71 billion in the same period last year.
Social Security Bank was up five at 1,030 cedis.
Offers exceeded bids by 1,235,980 shares to 315,020 and 204,980 shares were traded compared to 57,560 on Wednesday.
Ghana's year-on-year inflation rate fell to 54.2 percent in May, the fifth successive monthly drop, according to provisional figures released by the national statistics service.
Inflation peaked at 70.8 percent in December but has been falling since then.
